structured_output.what_is_happening: Within about an hour, more than ten Solana tokens named "Effective Accelerationism / e/acc" were launched. They seem to point back to a post by @beffjezos (status 2103593870189858971, taken from the GeckoTerminal twitter field). I could not read the post because X returned HTTP 402. This token (6rTrEf…) is a direct Meteora pair, not from a launchpad, created at 22:00 UTC. It is one of the later clones. It has gone up about 10x in 10 minutes to roughly $125k mcap, with $1.26M of volume. The oldest clone, CbcyNo…, is already at about $1.1M mcap, and several others sit between $360k and $870k.

narrative.description: e/acc (effective accelerationism) is the tech/AI movement led by Beff Jezos (Guillaume Verdon, founder of Extropic). A post from the Beff account appears to have set off a burst of token launches. The meme and the figure are well known in crypto and AI circles.
narrative.why_spreading: A post by a well-known figure appears to have set off a wave of copycat launches. The name is recognisable and has crossover with crypto (Bankless and Pirate Wires appearances). I could not read the post, so I cannot confirm he endorsed any token.

token_connection.why_this_token: It has only the shared name and ticker. It is not the first launch (the first was CbcyNo… at 21:15 UTC, about 45 minutes earlier) and it is not the market leader. I found no official link or endorsement.
token_connection.competing_tokens: At least 10 same-name tokens: CbcyNo… ($1.1M mcap, the earliest in this wave), 3m7Bhp… ($873k), DseCuJ… ($556k), 7dVWLA… ($362k, $8.7M h1 volume), 13vVSQ… ($223k, $267k liquidity), FHxEUq… (newer), and an older 2024 pump.fun e/acc.

authenticity.evidence: GMGN flags 74 bundler wallets, and bundlers account for about 67% of top-trader activity. There are 1,569 unique buyers but only 78 unique sellers, a pattern consistent with bot or bundled buying. Top-10 holders own about 21% (GeckoTerminal's 72% probably includes the pool). There are no paid boosts, no smart-money wallets and no KOL wallets. The attention is real at the name level, but this particular clone's flow looks largely manufactured.
authenticity.uncertainty: I could not see X, so I don't know whether anyone is promoting this specific contract address.

structural_risks: 100% of LP is unlocked on a Meteora pool the deployer created, so liquidity can be pulled at any time
A low number of LP providers
74 bundler wallets, with bundlers making up about 67% of top-trader activity
About 10 competing clones splitting the attention, with the leaders already priced 3-9x higher
Already up about 10x in 10 minutes, so the entry comes after the vertical move

structured_output.counterargument: Clone swarms tied to a real famous-figure post can lift the lagging clones as the leader climbs; a leader at $1.1M suggests room for $250k+ clones. Liquidity is relatively deep at $72k against a $125k mcap, buyers far outnumber sellers, and mint and freeze authority are renounced. If this clone becomes the "cheap e/acc", doubling from $125k is plausible within hours.

Whether the deployer will pull the unlocked Meteora liquidity

Who the deployer is (GMGN shows no prior tokens)

source_coverage.notes: The X status fetch returned 402. A search on the contract address returned nothing. A web search on Beff Jezos e/acc turned up only background material about the movement, nothing about a token. Time was too short to cover Reddit, Telegram and Discord.

structured_output.thesis: This is a late, non-canonical clone in a swarm of e/acc copies. The dev's liquidity is fully unlocked, bundling is heavy, and the buy/sell pattern looks bot-driven. The narrative has some pull, but this token has no claim to it and it has already made a 10x vertical move. The rug risk is high, and a 2x before -50% is below average for the pool.
